clue.text: Disruptive worker at Apple gathering?

parts.note: a worker is a classic crossword ant, the toiling insect of the colony
Apple names its products with a lower-case i prefix (iPhone, iPad), so whatever is at Apple is an I
a social is an informal party or get-together

explanation.surface: A troublemaking employee at a tech company's staff party.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful idea that Apple branding adds an i to anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour that harms or disturbs other people is called antisocial, a near synonym for disruptive.

clue.text: Take in muscles on heavenly body?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so on puts this before what follows

parts.note: abs is the short name for the abdominal muscles
an orb is a sphere, poetically a sun, moon or planet

explanation.surface: A query about exercising one's stomach muscles atop a celestial sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To absorb something is to soak it up or take it in, whether liquid or information.

clue.text: Priorities of treatment room in any given emergency

definitions.meaning: the sorting of patients by urgency so the most serious are treated first
the assessment area of a hospital emergency department where arrivals are first sorted

explanation.surface: A medical note on what comes first, and where, when an emergency strikes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals use the word both for ranking patients by need and for the assessment room where that happens.

clue.text: Egocentric leftist sneered outrageously

indicators.note: something done outrageously is wild and out of order, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed left-winger sneering scandalously at others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges all fourteen letters of LEFTIST SNEERED.
explanation.definitionFit: An egocentric person thinks of their own advantage first, which is the meaning of being concerned with one's own gain.

clue.text: Left coalition to support business partner

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so these words place what comes before them on top

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
a league is an alliance or coalition of parties

explanation.surface: A left-wing alliance backing a commercial firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts L and LEAGUE beneath CO in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A colleague is someone you work alongside, a partner in the same enterprise.

clue.text: Turn in battlefield data following uprising

indicators.note: in a down light an uprising means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
the letters sit in the run of the words battlefield data

explanation.surface: Twisting the figures from a battle report after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds ELDDA spanning battlefiELD DAta; 'uprising' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk or eggs that turn have gone bad, which is the old sense of addle: to spoil or go rotten.

clue.text: Score draw lacking slick wingers

indicators.note: lacking means the following letters are missing from the word before

parts.note: to draw is to sketch

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so the slick wingers are the outer letters of slick

explanation.surface: A football result: a draw in a match where neither side had flashy wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of slick are S and K; lacking those, SKETCH loses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, just as etching engraves lines.

clue.text: In-depth, hard or difficult cases

indicators.note: difficult cases means the word for difficult encloses what precedes it

parts.note: tough means difficult
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A description of complex legal cases explored in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like a noun for legal matters, but here it is a verb meaning encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough investigation is a detailed, exhaustive one, the sense of in-depth.

clue.text: Note over telephone lines in inn

indicators.note: in a down clue over means read upwards, so the note is turned round

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
RY, for railway, is the crossword abbreviation for lines of track

explanation.surface: A message left by phone for someone staying at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an old-fashioned word for a pub or inn offering food and lodging.

clue.text: Order in Costa for a change to sandwich place

indicators.note: to sandwich is to enclose a filling between two outer parts
letters altered for a change are rearranged into another order

parts.note: a station is a place or post where someone is stationed

explanation.surface: Choosing a sandwich in a Costa coffee shop for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges IN COSTA to ACTIONS; 'to sandwich' puts the place between its sixth and seventh letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a military command telling troops to take up battle positions, so it is an order.

clue.text: Upset odds badly

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A gambler annoyed that the odds went poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset a drink is to knock it over, which is to spill it.

clue.text: Farcical, ridiculous organisation, one I ignored

indicators.note: organisation is the act of arranging things, so the letters are put in a new order
ignored means left out of the word

parts.note: the word has two letter Is and only one of them goes

explanation.surface: Complaint about an absurd company that took no notice of the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops one I from RIDICULOUS; 'organisation' rearranges the nine letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical and ludicrous are synonyms, both meaning absurd enough to laugh at.

clue.text: Kind of jazz artist with good rhythm

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's usual artist
time is the rhythm or beat of music

explanation.surface: A painter who can also keep a steady beat in a jazz band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is an early, syncopated style of piano music that is a forerunner and kind of jazz.

clue.text: Detective's turf in drugs incident

indicators.note: in places what precedes it within the drugs

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so two of them are EE
a PI is a private investigator, a detective; the 's ties him to the turf
sod is a piece of turf

explanation.surface: A private eye's patch caught up in the narcotics trade.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is a single event or occurrence, which is what an incident is.

clue.text: East German plays collecting silver for theatre worker

indicators.note: collecting means taking in and holding the next item
letters that play about are free to move, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A Cold War dramatist picking up an award for their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' turns EAST GERMAN into STAGEMANER, which 'collecting' opens to take in AG before the final ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The person running the stage during a performance, cueing lights and scene changes, is a backstage theatre job.

clue.text: Damage on top of wall essentially made of marble

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
on top of means in addition to, that is, more

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence, the core, so the middle letters of wall are taken

explanation.surface: Vandalism to a wall that turns out to be made of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmoreal is a literary adjective from the Latin for marble, describing something of or like it.

clue.text: 'Steal' present on holiday

parts.note: to present something is to give it
someone on holiday is away

explanation.surface: A gift for someone while they are off on vacation, or a robbery while they're out.
explanation.definitionFit: A steal is a bargain so cheap it is almost free, which is what a giveaway price means.

clue.text: Improve upon passage in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as said aloud, so the spoken words stand for a different spelling

parts.note: upon means over, and a passage or corridor is a hall

explanation.surface: A writer's note to polish a passage within a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul a machine is to examine and repair it thoroughly, improving it.

clue.text: Weak, short Italian beer, tavern served up

indicators.note: things served up are dished out in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: It is the short form of Italian

explanation.surface: A disappointing small Italian lager poured at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Spineless, literally lacking a backbone, is the figurative sense meaning weak or feeble in character.

clue.text: Decent holds for climbing spot

indicators.note: holds means the first word contains what follows

parts.note: nice means pleasant or decent

indicators.note: in a down light climbing means reading upwards, so the little word is turned round

parts.note: to and for both express purpose or direction

explanation.surface: A climber praising the good handholds on a route.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbers' 'holds' and 'spot' look like a rock wall; here 'holds' is containment and 'spot' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to catch sight of it, to notice it.

clue.text: Failing to transfer allegiance

definitions.meaning: a noun: a flaw or shortcoming
to switch sides, abandoning one country or party for another

explanation.surface: A weakness that drives someone to switch sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fault or failing; the verb is to desert to the other side, changing loyalty.

clue.text: Bloc of countries rejecting American savings scheme with regret

indicators.note: rejecting means sending back, so the run is read in reverse

parts.note: an ISA, an Individual Savings Account, is a British tax-free savings scheme
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Nations turning down a US pension plan and wishing they hadn't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns the whole run A ISA RUE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass joining Europe and Asia is a vast grouping of countries, and the name of a superstate in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.

clue.text: Miss that's eager to embrace love

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the eager word wraps round the next

parts.note: avid means keen or eager
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A young woman keen to find romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a young woman; it is a verb, to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something, such as a traffic jam, is to escape or sidestep it.

clue.text: Reveal and enter result

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal something about them publicly
to come in, or come, is to enter a room

explanation.surface: Instructions to disclose something and then go in, whatever happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The outcome of an event is its result or consequence.

clue.text: Sort of filter in whole bean extraction?

indicators.note: extraction pulls things out and apart, so the letters are rearranged; the query flags the coffee joke

explanation.surface: Coffee-making: a filter for brewing from whole beans.
explanation.walkthrough: Baleen whales strain krill through plates of this material, so it is a natural filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Baleen, the horny plates in some whales' mouths, strains food from seawater, acting as a filter.

clue.text: Suggest son must leave work function

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: must leave means this letter goes out of the word

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boss hinting that their son must quit the work party.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, to put a view forward, much as one suggests.

clue.text: Shout of the old liberals

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe
L is the abbreviation for Liberal, so two are LL

explanation.surface: A rallying cry from the old Liberal party faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud cry, a shout.

clue.text: Perhaps minor benefit in a small amount of money?

indicators.note: in places the benefit within the rest

parts.note: a cent is a coin, a small sum of money
the dole is state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A child's pocket money topped up with a state handout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that a minor is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor, someone under adult age, is often a teenager, so a minor may be a youth in that stage.
